shared_qualifications: C1: same mV(SCE) scale throughout; no electrode offset. C2 for explicitly binary Al–X: wt%X=100*x*M_X/[x*M_X+(100−x)*26.982], with x in at.%; inversely CRA-derived at%X=100*(w_X/M_X)/(w_X/M_X+w_Al/26.982). Atomic weights Al26.982, Nb92.906, Mo95.95, Cr51.996, W183.84 from CIAAW https://ciaaw.org/abridged-atomic-weights.htm . CRA-derived atomic percentages are calculations from supplied cells, not independent paper analyses. Both original cells are retained.

PDF pp.2–3: sputter-deposited binary thin films, stagnant air-exposed .1 M NaCl, SCE; current tests scan 1 mV/s to a stable pit then step down for growth/repassivation. Earlier reference-3 fresh measurements used pH10 and .2 mV/s. Current solution numerical pH and test temperature are not stated; CRA pH7 and 25°C are unverified. CRA pH10 is not reliable evidence of aging state: its values often resemble aged rather than earlier fresh results.

Fresh, aged and repassivation symbols are distinct. Fresh Nb points are cited experimental averages; Mo fresh present-versus-cited origin is unresolved; fresh Cr includes cited and newly deposited points. These classifications are preserved. Air aging is not a heat-treatment anneal. No aggregate is manufactured from scattered aged points or the CRA Avg header.

CRA Nos.743/744 have negative targets (−750/−875) near the magnitudes of positive aged Nb results. This suggests possible sign errors but does not establish identity or authorize correction; affected assignments remain candidates. Nb No.746 may instead resemble an unregistered repassivation value, so no supported pitting link is forced.

CRA converted compositions often differ from registered graphical coordinates: e.g. Nb≈5/15/26 versus source4.3/15.5/26.6 at.%, Mo≈5 versus6, Cr≈5 versus6 and ≈38 versus39.5. These differences are disclosed in paired evidence. Clearer composition conflicts retain candidates rather than silently replacing source coordinates.

Candidates involving nearby fresh/aged values, possible sign errors or growth-curve endpoints are alternatives only. Multiple IDs/observations in a candidate group do not imply duplicate runs or a database mean. Supported matches alone are suitable for default joins.

PDF p.9 explicitly identifies highest potential on each downward-stepping growth curve as its pitting/start potential. Figures 5–6 can repeat Figure 1/4 populations but do not establish individual aging/run identities; candidate links retain that limitation. The cited Al–5.2 at.% W >800 mV bound (obs_030) remains separate from the present −60 mV result (obs_040).
